post.caption: Germans named eyeglasses after a gemstone. The German word for glasses is Brille, and it comes from the Latin word for beryl. Beryl is the mineral behind emerald and aquamarine. Before glasses, people used polished beryl or rock crystal to read, and the first eyeglasses came from Italy in the late 1200s. Around 1306, a friar said they were less than twenty years old. In medieval Latin, the word for beryl came to mean eyeglass too. Glass lenses later replaced the stone ones, and the element beryllium is named after beryl as well.
